# Ticket Reopened

`customer_support.sit.ticket_reopened` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `customer_support.diagnosis_and_resolution.verification_and_closure`


> Something we declared resolved was not resolved, and the customer has come back to say so. The correct first move is not to answer again — it is to work out which of four categorically different failures this is, because they carry opposite lessons and averaging them into a reopen rate is why that metric is useless in most organisations. It was never fixed (closure without verification, usually an auto-close on silence). It fixed the wrong problem (a diagnosis error, and the most instructive of the four). It was fixed and regressed (a product defect, and not a support failure at all). Or it was fixed for some cases and not others (a scope error, which means other customers are affected and have not written in). The second attempt also starts from a worse position than the first: the customer's patience is already spent and their belief that anyone is tracking their problem is already damaged, so the reply has to acknowledge the first attempt before it does anything else. Answering a reopen as though it were a fresh question is the response most likely to produce an escalation.

> Only followup_sent is a real substrate observation kind. reproduction_confirmed, root_cause_identified, ticket_resolved, ticket_reopened, escalation_requested, angry_language and cancellation_threat are support-native and sit in planned_substrate.obs_kinds. These lists are unvalidated, so the mixture is legal — recorded here so nobody reads it as coverage.
ticket_reopened appears in both the pending binding and signals_of_decay. That is deliberate and not a copy-paste: the trigger is the first reopen, and a FURTHER reopen while this situation is live is the decay signal, because it means the second attempt failed too. Second reopens are where a support relationship actually breaks, and they are the strongest available argument for changing who works the ticket rather than how.
The backward-invalidation described in the header is not something this file can perform. Layer 3 states that a reopen impeaches the resolution and the artifact that produced it; actually lowering a knowledge article's or an inference pattern's confidence is Layer 6's job, and it needs the closure's artifact ids carried on the ticket_reopened observation to do it. If the support pack ships this type without those ids, the loop stays open and this situation delivers a fraction of what it is for. That dependency should be recorded on the backlog item, not discovered afterwards.
